sections.label: Official Assignee as trustee
sections.summary: Private trustees were seldom appointed, and the Official Assignee acted as trustee in over 99% of bankruptcies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As a result, private trustees were seldom appointed and the Official Assignee, or the OA, was appointed to act as the trustee in over 99% of bankruptcies.

sections.label: PTIBs to administer bankruptcies
sections.summary: The Bill mandates PTIBs administer all bankruptcy cases except those the OA decides to administer for public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of end-2021, PTIBs administer about 40% of bankruptcy cases, with the OA administering the remaining 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Based on feedback from the industry, the experience of PTIBs undertaking the administration of bankruptcy cases that are filed by ICs has generally been smooth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This Bill will now seek to introduce changes to the bankruptcy regime: to mandate that PTIBs now administer all bankruptcy cases, except those which the OA will decide to administer, having regard to public interest.

sections.label: Consent required for bankruptcy order
sections.summary: Clause 6 introduces section 318A barring a bankruptcy order unless a PTIB or the OA consents to act as trustee.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To complement these amendments, clause 6 introduces a new section 318A to provide that the Court must not make a bankruptcy order if a PTIB or the OA has not consented to act as the trustee in bankruptcy.

sections.label: Undischarged bankrupt deposit offence
sections.summary: Clause 10 makes it an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to receive a deposit of at least $10,000 without disclosing bankruptcy status.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, clause 10 introduces a new section 412(1)(d), which makes it an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to receive a deposit of at least $10,000 from any such person if he or she – the bankrupt	– does not disclose his or her bankruptcy status to that person.

sections.label: Public access to employment information
sections.summary: Clause 11 amends section 433(1) to let the public obtain information undischarged bankrupts submitted to the OA on employment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Next, clause 11 will amend section 433(1) to allow the public to obtain information that undischarged bankrupts have submitted to the OA regarding their current employment status and employment history.

sections.label: SIP company liquidations completed
sections.summary: As at 31 December 2022, the Official Receiver completed the liquidation of 27 companies under the SIP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As at 31 December 2022, the Official Receiver has completed the liquidation of 27 companies under the SIP.

sections.label: Validity period extended two years
sections.summary: Clauses 4 and 5 amend sections 72B(1) and 250B(1), extending the validity period by two years to 28 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clauses 4 and 5 thus amend sections 72B(1) and 250B(1), extending the validity period for an additional two years to 28 January 2026.

sections.label: Insolvency practitioners adopt SIP processes
sections.summary: The Ministry is looking at allowing insolvency practitioners, not just the Official Receiver, to adopt some of the SIP's simplified and expedited processes for eligible companies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, my Ministry is looking at allowing insolvency practitioners and not just the Official Receiver to adopt some of the SIP's simplified and expedited processes for the restructuring or winding up of eligible companies that are under their administration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This would, in turn, benefit more MSCs going forward.

sections.label: PTIBs appointed for other bankruptcies
sections.summary: The transformation would be completed by requiring PTIBs to be appointed for all other bankruptcies, about 60% of bankruptcies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Seen against this background, it makes sense to complete the transformation by requiring that for all other bankruptcies – I understand they are about 60% of bankruptcies, in respect of which PTIBs have not been appointed – PTIBs be now appointed too.

sections.label: No deposit asked from ICs
sections.summary: Their practice is generally not to ask for any deposit from the ICs, relying on the $1,850 deposit placed with the OA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Their practice, generally, is not to ask for any deposit from the ICs to cover their costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They rely on the $1,850 deposit placed with the OA when the person brings a bankruptcy application.

sections.label: Debtors must get PTIB practitioners
sections.summary: In this Bill, it is proposed that debtors must also get practitioners to be PTIBs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this Bill, it is proposed that debtors must also get practitioners to be PTIBs.

sections.label: OA consent as trustee
sections.summary: The question asks whether the OA would consider, case-by-case, whether it is in the public interest to consent to be trustee of the bankrupt's estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would the OA be willing to consider, on a case-by-case basis, whether it would be in the public interest to provide consent to be the trustee of the bankrupt's estate?

sections.label: OA duty to investigate bankrupts
sections.summary: Under section 22 of the IRDA, the OA must investigate the conduct and affairs of the bankrupt and check for offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Currently, under section 22 of the IRDA, the OA has a responsibility to investigate the conduct and affairs of the bankrupt, to check if the bankrupt has committed certain offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When the PTIB takes over these duties from the OA, how do we ensure that the PTIB will reasonably discharge these duties?

sections.label: PTIB fees and deemed consent
sections.summary: Clause 3 of the Bill deems creditors to consent to the PTIB's remuneration if they do not object within the prescribed time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These efficiencies, I believe, will have a direct impact in ensuring that PTIBs' fees will not become excessive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I particularly commend the provision of the default position in clause 3 of the Bill allowing creditors to have deemed to consent to the remuneration sought by the PTIB in the "prescribed manner", if they did not raise objection within the prescribed time.

sections.label: List of undischarged bankrupts
sections.summary: Clause 11 requires the OA to maintain a list of undischarged bankrupts with employment history and current employment status particulars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Clause 11 of the Bill provides for the OA to maintain a list of undischarged bankrupts with records of the particulars of the employment history of every undischarged bankrupt, as well as the particulars of his current employment status.

sections.label: Private sector and incentives
sections.summary: The passage says the private sector may carry out some work reliably if an architecture of incentives makes PTIBs serve the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the private sector can carry out some of this in a reliable way, there is good reason for us to consider this as a viable option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The key is to ensure that we set up an architecture of incentives, so that the PTIBs, even as they pursue private commercial ends, bend to the public interest as their key performance indicator.

sections.label: 2015 institutional creditor amendment
sections.summary: In 2015 the Bankruptcy Act was amended to require institutional creditors to have bankrupt debtors' estates managed by PTIBs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A major change took place in 2015, when the then-Bankruptcy Act was amended to require institutional creditors, such as banks and finance companies to have their bankrupt debtors estates managed by PTIBs.

sections.label: All creditors must appoint PTIB
sections.summary: The Bill requires all creditors, not just institutional ones, to appoint a PTIB to make a debtor bankrupt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill before the House today will move the needle further as it proposes that all creditors, not just institutional creditors, will need to appoint a PTIB if they intend to make that debtors bankrupt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When the scheme in the Bill is implemented, the OA will directly manage only a minority of bankruptcies, which the Ministry has explained would be cases with a public interest element, such as when public funds have been misused.

sections.label: Ministry media release on PTIBs
sections.summary: The Ministry's 28 November media release stated PTIB bankruptcy administration since 2017 has been smooth with no action by the OA or Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Ministry's media release of 28 November, it was stated that the administration of bankruptcy estates by PTIBs since 2017, "has been smooth and no action has been taken on the PTIBs by the OA and/or the Courts on the PTIBs' management of bankruptcies." This was apparently based on feedback from the industry.

sections.label: Oversight of private trustees
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will ensure effective oversight and quality of private trustees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, how will the Ministry ensure the effective oversight and quality of private trustees?

sections.label: Court case on trustee review
sections.summary: In Zhang Hong En Jonathan's case, the Court found little statutory guidance on exercising its discretion when reviewing the private trustee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a recent High Court case of Zhang Hong En Jonathan against his private trustee, the Court found little guidance in the statute over how it should exercise its discretion when exercising its review powers over the trustee.

sections.label: No private trustee available
sections.summary: The question asks what happens if no private trustee is reasonably available to act in the bankruptcy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What happens if no private trustee is reasonably available to act in the bankruptcy?

sections.label: Monitoring bankruptcy trends after collapses
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry is monitoring and preparing for changing bankruptcy trends after Terra and FTX collapsed amid high inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister share whether the Ministry is monitoring and preparing for changing trends in bankruptcies following the collapse of Terra and FTX, especially in a backdrop of high inflation?

sections.label: PTIBs share of bankruptcy cases
sections.summary: PTIBs currently handle almost 50% of bankruptcy administration and will likely cover almost 100% except public interest cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, PTIBs handle almost 50% of the administration of bankruptcy cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With this Bill, they will likely cover almost 100% of those cases except for cases involving public interest.

sections.label: Undischarged bankrupt deposit offence
sections.summary: New section 412(1)(d) makes it an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to receive at least $10,000 without disclosing bankruptcy status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new section 412(1)(d) makes it an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to receive a deposit of at least $10,000 from any person if he or she does not disclose his or her bankruptcy status to that person.

sections.label: Publicly searchable bankrupt information
sections.summary: New section 433(1) enhances the amount of publicly searchable information about undischarged bankrupts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, on the new section 433(1), which enhances the amount of publicly searchable information about undischarged bankrupts.

sections.label: One-stop searchable bankruptcy database
sections.summary: A one-stop searchable database is suggested to include pending bankruptcy applications and details of an undischarged bankrupt's PTIB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, if I may humbly suggest a one-stop searchable database which would include pending bankruptcy applications and details of an undischarged bankrupt's PTIB, so as to allow the public member to conduct further due diligence on not only that person, but the PTIB in question.

sections.label: Thanking MinLaw for Bill
sections.summary: The speaker thanks MinLaw for pushing the Bill forward to achieve efficient outcomes and justice for creditors, the public, debtors and bankrupts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I want to thank MinLaw for pushing forward this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill will help us to achieve more efficient outcomes and effect justice not just for creditors, not just for members of the public, but also for debtors and bankrupts alike.

sections.label: OA bankruptcy administration figures
sections.summary: The OA has historically administered a large number of bankruptcies, with figures of 99% originally and 60% presently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The OA has historically administered a large number of bankruptcies – I think the figures revealed by the Minister were 99% originally and 60% presently.

sections.label: PTIB default bankruptcy administration
sections.summary: The legislation creates a default that the PTIB will administer all bankruptcies, with the applicant identifying the professional before applying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In that sense, I can see where this legislation is coming from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is creating, as a default, that the PTIB will administer all bankruptcies and the burden is on the applicant applying for bankruptcy to identify the professional before the application can be made.

sections.label: Difficulty finding PTIBs for small estates
sections.summary: Requiring a PTIB per bankruptcy may make it hard to find professionals willing to administer smaller estates at an economic price, especially when the bankrupt applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The main downside of requiring a PTIB to be appointed for each bankruptcy is that it may be difficult to find professionals who are prepared to administer smaller estates at an economic price, particularly where the applicant is the bankrupt himself.

sections.label: Safeguards when PTIBs decline appointments
sections.summary: Borrowing to repay old debts balloons debts, harming borrowers and lenders, and the Minister is asked about safeguards when PTIBs decline appointments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This borrowing to repay old debts generally leads to the ballooning of debts, which are detrimental both to borrowers and lenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would be grateful if the Minister can share whether there are any safeguards, particularly for those cases where the PTIBs may not be willing to take up an appointment, to ensure that those who otherwise qualify for bankruptcy will still be able to take out the appropriate applications.

sections.label: Eligible versus acting PTIBs
sections.summary: Of the total, 183 are eligible to take up bankruptcy administration now, but only about 56, about a third, currently do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Of this, the vast majority – 183 of them – are eligible to take up bankruptcy administration at present, but only about a third of them – about 56 – currently do so.

sections.label: PTIB list on Insolvency Office website
sections.summary: A list of PTIBs will be put on the Insolvency Office's website so information about them is accessible to those filing bankruptcy claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Lim also asked on whether information about the PTIBs could be made accessible and how would someone who wants to file a bankruptcy claim can access that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will put a list of the PTIBs on the Insolvency Office's website.

sections.label: Bankruptcy filing fee unchanged
sections.summary: The threshold for the filing fee, the bankruptcy fee, of $1,850 has not changed with these amendments being introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Murali observed that debtors may face problems applying for bankruptcy, I presume, after these amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But I want to assure Mr Murali that the threshold for the filing fee, the bankruptcy fee, of $1,850 has not changed with these amendments being introduced.

sections.label: Regulatory framework for PTIB duties
sections.summary: The Ministry has put in place a robust regulatory framework to ensure PTIBs perform their duties faithfully and observe all statutory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Ministry has put in place a robust regulatory framework to ensure that PTIBs perform their duties faithfully and observe all statutory requirements relating to the performance of their duties.

sections.label: Undischarged bankruptcy cases decrease
sections.summary: From 2011 to 2022, total undischarged bankruptcy cases fell 63%, from 25,028 to 9,254.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2022, the total number of undischarged bankruptcy cases decreased by 63% from 25,028 cases in 2011 to 9,254 cases in 2022.

sections.label: Complaints against PTIBs management
sections.summary: Complaints about PTIBs' management of bankruptcy cases since 2016 were looked into, and none were misconduct cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, it is an adversarial process, so there are bound to be cases where interests differ or compete, and it is inevitable that there will be conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There have been complaints raised to the OA on PTIBs' management of bankruptcy cases since 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I am sure many of us have come across those cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We received complaints like that, that the OA or the PTIB is too tough and asking for too much and so on, but we have looked into all of them, and none of them are misconduct cases.

sections.label: PTIBs investigation powers
sections.summary: Powers of investigation and prosecution are not devolved to PTIBs and remain with the OA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Murali raised concerns over how we can ensure the PTIBs have reasonably discharged duties that involve investigations into the conduct and affairs of the bankrupt, to check if offences have been committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that these powers of investigation and, indeed, of prosecution are not devolved to PTIBs, and so, that remains within the province of the OA.

sections.label: PTIBs fees approval
sections.summary: PTIBs' fees have to be approved by the creditors or the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: PTIBs' fees also have to be approved by the creditors or the Court.

sections.label: Undisclosed bankruptcy deposit offence
sections.summary: A $10,000 per transaction deposit is an offence if a bankrupt does not disclose bankruptcy status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: You might recall that I said $10,000 per transaction would be considered an offence if the bankrupt dealing with a person in a commercial transaction does not disclose that he or she is a bankrupt in taking the deposit.

sections.label: Deposit threshold and habitual patterns
sections.summary: Section 412(1)(d) is not committed if each deposit is under $10,000, but habitual patterns may lead to offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, whilst an offence under the proposed section 412(1)(d) will not be committed so long as each individual deposit collected does not exceed $10,000, but I think Mr Zhulkarnain also knows that if you are a bankrupt and you keep collecting as a habitual pattern smaller amounts under $10,000, there is a pattern of doing so – not disclosing your bankruptcy status, which is not an offence, but then you disguise that fact and you use the deposit for some other purposes, and because you are a bankrupt, it causes a loss to the person who has paid the deposit – then I am sure Mr Zhulkarnain knows that the OA would then have the ability to look into that conduct and there will be offences connected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, this enhancement is designed only to deal with notification when you collect the deposit and we set the threshold at $10,000.

sections.label: Employment information in service
sections.summary: The amendments will include employment information in this service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: With the amendments, we will include employment information in this service as well.

sections.label: PTIB filing statement of affairs
sections.summary: A PTIB who gets the statement of affairs can file it even if commercial interest is not aligned with public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The point I sought to make, and I apologise if it was not clear, was that when a PTIB gets the statement of affairs, if the commercial interest is not aligned with public interest, he can just file it, even though with some level of due diligence, he could unearth reasonable suspicion of offences, which then the OA may be interested in to formally investigate and prosecute, depending on the evidence.

sections.label: Administration recovery of assets
sections.summary: The administration deals with the same end outcome of better and more efficient recovery of assets from the bankrupt's estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Fundamentally, the administration deals with the same end outcome – which is better and more efficient recovery of assets from the bankrupt's estate.

sections.label: OA investigation powers continue
sections.summary: The statement of affairs and regular reports go to the OA, whose investigation powers continue to lie with him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Murali Pillai knows that the statement of affairs as well as regular reports are provided to the OA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And, in those cases, I am sure the OA will, if his interest is piqued by any of these reports or findings, take steps to further investigate, and the powers of the investigation, and indeed, any other matters which aid the investigations, still continue to lie with the OA.
